observations.body: Matthew’s courtyard account moves from a servant girl to bystanders, from denial to oath and cursing, and from crowing to remembered words.
observations.label: Then he began to curse and swear

observations.body: The passage presents Denial, oath, cursing, remembering, and weeping as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Denial, oath, cursing, remembering, and weeping

observations.body: The passage places Peter beside Denial, oath, cursing, remembering, and weeping.
observations.label: Peter

payload.posture: Read Matthew 26:69–75 as one movement in Peter's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states matthew’s courtyard account moves from a servant girl to bystanders, from denial to oath and cursing, and from crowing to remembered words. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Peter's story.
payload.title: Then he began to curse and swear
